Stage-02 : Modelling Transformation

Cube object without light 
❖Once 3D modelling is done, each part of the object needs to be filled with 
colour.
❖Objects are visible in presence of light, and depending on the position of light 
source, objects may appear differently.
❖In 3D world, multiple light sources may be available, so their cumulative effect 
needs to be synthesized to give a real effect.
Cube object with light

❖ In this lighting process, the task is to mimic the optical phenomenon of

Stage-04 : Viewing Transformation

❖First, we need to set-up a camera also known as setting view co-ordinate 
system. 
❖Then, the world coordinate scene (3D-colour scene) is transformed to view 
co-ordinate system. This step is known as View Transformation.
It is similar to take a 
snapshot of a 3D

Stage-04 (Sub-stage-02) : Viewing 
Transformation

❖ For projection, we defined a region in view co-ordinate space called view 
volume.  
❖ All the objects inside the view volume are projected on the view plane. So, 
objects outside the view volume can’t be projected.
❖ For example: Green ball is outside the view volume, and so it is not projected 
on view plane.

❖ In addition to the above transformation, this stage required two more 
operations known as Clipping and Hidden surface removal.

❖ Display screen is a continuous space comprises of discrete grids of elements 
called pixel grid.
❖ However, values obtained at the viewport level may not be discrete (it is 
continuous), and so the obtained values need to be suitably approximated to 
nearest digital values, so that it can be viewed on the screen.
(0,0)
Stage-05 : Scan Conversion

❖ Approximation should be done in such a way that minimum distortion can 
occur on the screen. 
❖ Anti-aliasing methods were used to avoid distortion on the screen.

Graphics Pipeline Implementation
❖ As a graphics programmer, we need actually to implement each of the 
stages of Computer Graphics pipeline to synthesize an image on screen. 
❖ As it is very time consuming as well effortful process.
❖ Rather, its better to use some of the existing libraries such as:
❖OpenGL – open source graphics library : This library facilitates so many 
already implemented graphics functions such as. 
❖glVertex2f(-0.8f, 0.1f) 
❖glColor3f(1.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);   // Red
❖glColor3f(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);   // Green
❖ glColor3f(0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);   // Blue
❖ Simplify the life as a graphics programmer regardless of knowing each and 
every theoretical aspect of Computer Graphics pipeline.

Practice Problem - 01
▪
Question – 01: In object representation, individual object is represented 
with respect to:
(A) Local coordinate system
(B) Camera coordinate system
(C) Global coordinate system
(D) World coordinate system
(E) None

Practice Problem - 02
▪
Question – 02 : In Computer Graphics, clipping refers to:
(A) The process of converting 3D objects into 2D images
(B) The process of removing parts of objects that lie outside the viewing region
(C) The process of mapping objects from world coordinates to device coordinates
(D) The process of filling polygons with colors or textures
(E) Both (B) and (C)

Practice Problem - 03
▪
Question – 03 : Removing invisible parts of objects that fall outside the 
defined viewing area, before rasterization.
(A) Clipping
(B) Hidden Surface Removal
(C) Editing
(D) Clamping
(E) None

Practice Problem - 04
▪
Question – 04 : Rendering in computer graphics primarily refers to:
(A) Converting 3D objects into wireframe models
(B) Removing hidden surfaces from an image
(C) Generating a 2D image from a 3D scene description
(D) Mapping coordinates from world space to device space
(E) None
